Players bid to become the soloist, with the bid level determining how many cards they can exchange from the 'talon' (3, 2, 1, or none). The soloist's goal is to win at least 6 of the 11 tricks, often while attempting the challenging 'ArrivÃ¡zs'â€”winning the final three tricks.

First documented in 1990 by JÃ³zsef Pais in 'Ulti, Tarokk Ã©s nÃ©hÃ¡ny kis jÃ¡tÃ©k', Asszorti is believed to be a simplified hybrid designed to bridge the gap between complex Tarokk games and standard Whist variants.
Three players. No partnerships; the highest bidder becomes the declarer and plays alone against the other two defenders. Deal and play are clockwise.
36-card French-suited deck (remove 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s). Rank: A (high) > K > Q > J > 10 > 9 > 8 > 7 > 6.
Standard deck stripped to 36 cards, score sheet.
Deal 11 cards to each player. The remaining 3 cards form the face-down 'Talon'.

items.text: Open Talon: Discarded talon cards are shown to defenders.
